pages.text: Outputs are filled $(item)from the bottom up$() in the order below: the first product goes into the lowest output, the lightest into the highest.

$(l)6 outputs: 340 mB crude oil$()$(li)120 mB heavy oil$(li)60 mB diesel$(li)30 mB kerosene$(li)10 mB naphtha$(li)60 mB gasoline$(li)60 mB LPG$(br2)$(l)5 outputs: 330 mB crude oil$()$(br)Same as above $(item)without naphtha$(): 120 heavy oil, 60 diesel, 30 kerosene, 60 gasoline, 60 LPG.

$(l)3 outputs: 200 mB crude oil (light distillation)$()$(br)150 mB heavy oil, 45 mB diesel, 5 mB gasoline.$(br2)All amounts are per run at a heat of 2. The six-output tower gives the widest range of fuels, plus naphtha, which you need for plastics. The three-output tower is cheap to build but turns most of the oil into heavy oil.
